evidence.counting_rule: For each of the 44 probes, the Kotlin fragment required to satisfy the canonical_task (per support level FULL/PARTIAL, or excluded if NONE/no fragment) was checked against the frozen 9-item hidden-behavior checklist from semantic_compression.md section D (implicit conversions; hidden writable aliasing/mutation; overload/dynamic dispatch not locally evident; implicit allocation/copy/move/destroy/cleanup; implicit exception/failure propagation; hidden nullability/optionality; implicit representation change; context-dependent overflow/numeric behavior; hidden side effects on existing state). A probe is scored 1 raw hidden-cost unit if at least one checklist item applies to its fragment's surface form that is not made unambiguous by the fixed local syntax under the Kotlin language specification (per the 'do not count a behavior as hidden if fixed local syntax makes it unambiguous' rule); a probe is scored 0 if no such item applies. Probes with support level NONE for Kotlin (no fragment exists) are excluded from both numerator and denominator, consistent with the interaction_with_quality_metrics common-basis handling for metric D (this shard reports the Kotlin all-fragments figure only; common-basis recombination across all 10 languages is a runner-level aggregation step outside this single-language shard).
evidence.limitations: This is a single-worker desk audit of the Kotlin standard library and language specification against the frozen checklist, not a full 10-language empirical build/run pass. Every fragment's support level (FULL/PARTIAL/NONE) was inferred from documented Kotlin semantics rather than from an executed build under the frozen recipe; V1 (build-and-match) evidence was not independently re-executed in this packet-only shard. This limitation is recorded per spec 6.1.7 evidence-preservation requirements rather than silently omitted.
evidence.methodology_basis: capability_universe.json checklist D (Hidden Semantic Cost, 20% of quality score) applied per-probe to the fixed 44-probe universe for the fixed measured_fragment of each probe, per authoring rules R1-R10 and the support rubric. Higher normalized score = lower hidden semantic cost = better.

none_justification.F20.P1: Kotlin/JVM has no built-in FFI mechanism to call a native C function (int abs(int)) without a third-party binding generator (e.g. JNI requires hand-written native glue code and a separate build step, or a library such as JNA); this violates R7 (no external packages, no separate toolchain) and the frozen recipe's no-third-party-dependency baseline condition. N-1/N-2 apply.
none_justification.F20.P2: Kotlin/JVM produces JVM bytecode (a .jar) under its frozen recipe, not a native object file exposing an unmangled C-ABI symbol; there is no documented standard mechanism to export a C-callable symbol named exactly add2 discoverable by nm. N-1 applies; nm evidence: 'no compiled artifact under the frozen recipe' per NA rule for F20.P2.

evidence.normalization_note: Score direction follows the frozen rule 'lower hidden semantic cost is better' -> higher normalized score = better (fewer hidden behaviors). This is a single-language (Kotlin) shard; cross-language common-basis recombination for metric D is a runner-level step performed after all language shards are merged and is out of scope for this work unit.

per_probe_citations.F02.P2: ByteArray(16) is documented to zero-initialize; genuinely uninitialized storage is unavailable, so the substituted fragment (R9) silently produces zero-filled bytes rather than truly indeterminate contents -> implicit representation/initialization behavior not evident at the call site.
per_probe_citations.F03.P1: Kotlin Int arithmetic (x++/x+=1) wraps silently on overflow with no compiler flag or checked-mode operator in the standard recipe; overflow_exceptional_numeric behavior is not visible at the increment site.
per_probe_citations.F03.P2: MutableList indexed assignment (xs[1]=42) can throw IndexOutOfBoundsException; the possible_failure is not signaled at the assignment syntax.
per_probe_citations.F04.P1: Kotlin has no writable-reference/pointer form for a scalar local; the only standard workaround (single-element array or a mutable wrapper object) hides the true aliasing mechanism behind ordinary indexing/field syntax.
per_probe_citations.F04.P2: List.subList()/asList() style views share backing storage without copying, but this is not distinguishable from a copying operation by the call-site syntax alone.
per_probe_citations.F05.P1: Kotlin's bare call f(x) passes a MutableList reference; from the call-site alone a reader cannot tell whether the callee reads, mutates, resizes, or retains the alias.
per_probe_citations.F05.P2: Since Kotlin lacks primitive var pass-by-reference, the explicit form requires wrapping the Int in a mutable holder object; the wrapper masks that ordinary Kotlin call syntax elsewhere never grants write access to caller locals.
per_probe_citations.F05.P3: Kotlin lambdas/closures capturing an enclosing var box the captured variable (a Ref object) implicitly; this heap allocation is invisible at the declaration site.
per_probe_citations.F06.P2: Returning a Pair<Int,Int> from divmod2 allocates a Pair object; the call site binding (q,r) via destructuring hides that an intermediate object was allocated and destructured.
per_probe_citations.F07.P1: a*b+c on Int silently wraps on overflow with no local signal (checked-mode is not the Kotlin/JVM default and is not part of the frozen recipe).
per_probe_citations.F07.P2: Integer division truncates toward zero and % follows the dividend's sign for negative operands; this is a context-dependent rule not visible at the operator glyphs themselves.
per_probe_citations.F08.P1: Int + 1 at Int.MAX_VALUE wraps to Int.MIN_VALUE with no exception and no local marker of the checked-mode-vs-wrap distinction.
per_probe_citations.F08.P2: Integer division by zero throws ArithmeticException at runtime; this failure mode is not encoded in the operator or in the function's type.
per_probe_citations.F09.P1: Kotlin's == operator for strings calls .equals(), which is dynamically dispatched to a possibly user-overridden implementation; this indirection is not evident from the operator glyph.
per_probe_citations.F09.P2: sortedDescending() returns a new list rather than reordering in place, but a reader cannot tell copy-vs-mutate from the call syntax without consulting documentation.
per_probe_citations.F10.P1: Long.toInt() truncates high-order bits silently on out-of-range values with no local signal of the truncation.
per_probe_citations.F10.P2: Int + Double resolves via an overloaded Double.plus(Int) style stdlib operator that implicitly widens the Int operand; the widening conversion is invisible at the '+' site.
per_probe_citations.F11.P1: xs[i] on a List throws IndexOutOfBoundsException for an out-of-range i; this possible failure is not visible in the indexing syntax.
per_probe_citations.F11.P2: subList(1,4) returns a view backed by the original list's storage (not a copy); this sharing is not evident from the call syntax alone.
per_probe_citations.F13.P1: String.toInt() throws an unchecked NumberFormatException that is not declared in the function's signature (Kotlin has no checked exceptions), so the possible failure and its propagation path are invisible at the call site.
per_probe_citations.F13.P2: A try/catch fallback around toInt() hides which sub-expressions are 'protected' and what unwinding/cleanup occurs on the exceptional path from the construct's surface form alone.
per_probe_citations.F15.P1: A generic function over T is compiled with erasure for reference types but Kotlin autoboxes primitive T arguments (e.g. Int) at the generic call sites; this boxing is invisible in source.
per_probe_citations.F19.P1: Kotlin coroutines (async/await under runBlocking) use suspend-function continuation-passing transformation under the hood; control does not visibly 'leave' at the call site the way it would with an explicit thread launch.

evidence.score_formula: raw_total_hidden_units = sum(raw_hidden_cost_by_probe) = 23; denominator = probes_with_fragments_for_kotlin = 42 (each probe capped at 1 raw unit in this pass, i.e. presence/absence of any checklist-triggering hidden behavior rather than a full 9-category tally, to keep the count auditable and reproducible); normalized_score = 100 * (1 - raw_total_hidden_units / denominator) = 100 * (1 - 23/42) = 45.2, rounded to 45.
